stories.summary: El documento de 114 páginas de los socialistas contempla también un Pacto de Estado por la seguridad ferroviaria, un “escaño ciudadano” y la abolición de la prostitución

stories.summary: Han crecido viendo resquebrajarse el viejo mundo e intuyendo que les tocará poner en pie otro nuevo. Hablamos con 24 jóvenes nacidos en 2008 sobre sus ideas y preocupaciones

stories.title: La brújula infalible de Sigüés apunta a la derecha
stories.summary: Desde 1977, el partido que gana las elecciones generales en el pequeño pueblo aragonés es el que se impone en toda España. “No es descontento, es decepción”, coinciden exvotantes socialistas

stories.title: La ruta migratoria a Canarias bate su récord de llegadas en un solo día con más de 1.500 personas
stories.summary: El ministro Ángel Víctor Torres admite que el repunte es “muy importante” y que este año han llegado unas 17.000 personas a El Hierro, donde quedan ahora unas 1.600

stories.title: “Os deseo sufrimiento”: gloria y caída de Jensen Huang, rey de Nvidia, verso salvaje de la IA
stories.summary: La caída del gurú, en un caso de supuesto espionaje y adulterio, expone los riesgos de la concentración de poder en Estados Unidos

stories.title: "Quizás veamos el 25 de octubre de este año como el comienzo del fin de la recesión democrática mundial"
stories.summary: Larry Diamond, un reconocido experto internacional, dice en una entrevista que varios hechos recientes podrían indicar un cambio de patrón a favor de la democracia en el mundo.

stories.title: Los Lorenzana, Los Huistas y Los Mendoza: qué se sabe de las bandas criminales de Guatemala a las que EE.UU. designó como grupos terroristas extranjeros
stories.summary: Washington acusa a estos grupos de ser aliados de los carteles mexicanos de la droga y de colaborar con ellos en el tráfico de narcóticos.

stories.title: La mujer que lleva años atrapada en una isla paradisíaca sin poder volver a casa por un problema con su visa
stories.summary: Ruchira Ranasingha, de 50 años, lleva varada en las Islas Cook desde 2023 y quiere regresar a Sri Lanka.

stories.title: El legado de Miguel Ángel Asturias, el "olvidado" Nobel de Literatura guatemalteco al que los escritores del boom latinoamericano le dieron la espalda
stories.summary: Sus disputas con los autores del "boom" y su papel en el gobierno de Méndez Montenegro opacaron la obra Asturias poco después de recibir el Nobel.

stories.title: El efecto bouba/kiki, el extraordinario experimento psicológico que tiene los mismos resultados en casi todas las culturas
stories.summary: Es más que una curiosidad: podría ser una pista para develar el gran misterio de cómo empezamos a hablar.

stories.title: La conmoción en Panamá tras el ataque con explosivos contra la casa de un periodista
stories.summary: Rolando Rodríguez, el periodista cuya casa fue atacada, estaba investigando un presunto caso de corrupción en el país.

stories.title: "Las cortinas se pegaron al techo": cómo sobreviví al desastre de San Juanico, la explosión que dejó 650 muertos en México en 1984
stories.summary: Virginia Martínez Tellez es una de las sobrevivientes de uno de los desastres industriales más graves de la historia. Una fuga de gas en un depósito de la petrolera Pemex cambiaría para siempre su vida, la de su familia y la de toda una comunidad.

stories.title: Me dijeron que mi bebé había fallecido... 42 años después me envió un correo electrónico
stories.summary: Diane Sheehan tuvo a su primer hijo en 1976. Le dijeron que había muerto en el parto, pero no era cierto. Cuatro décadas después se enteró que estaba vivo.

stories.title: Por culpa de un viejo cable de cobre: qué se sabe de la suspensión de vuelos en EE.UU. más grande desde el 11S
stories.summary: Durante varias horas, permanecieron suspendidos en tierra todos los vuelos a lo largo del país. El secretario de Transportes llamó la atención sobre la necesidad de modernizar el sistema de control aéreo.

stories.title: Asere, corillo o chuchaqui: las palabras latinoamericanas que incorpora la nueva edición del Diccionario de la lengua española
stories.summary: Al diccionario se incorporaron 1.490 gentilicios y 1.570 voces de uso exclusivo en los distintos países hispanohablantes.

stories.title: Midterm voters ended the long-running GOP dominance in state legislatures
stories.summary: In several states, Democrats took control of legislatures that had been divided and they weakened GOP dominance in others. Issues on the agenda: More access to health care, new limits on school vouchers.

stories.title: A new generation of disability rights activists carry on Judy Heumann's legacy
stories.summary: The film Being Heumann tells the lesser-known story of the mother of the disability rights movement. A new generation of activists share how they "carry the torch" today.

stories.title: New Mexico wanted free childcare for all. This is what's worked — and what hasn't
stories.summary: A year ago in November, New Mexico became the first state to offer free childcare to every eligible family, regardless of income.

stories.title: Judge temporarily blocks Trump from moving ahead on Washington public golf course redevelopment
stories.summary: A federal judge on Saturday ordered a two-week delay to any work at a historic Washington public golf course not far from the White House.

stories.title: FAA ground stop disrupts college football
stories.summary: Some college football games were delayed a few hours on Saturday or postponed to Sunday. And in Oklahoma at least, there will be perks for fans to make up for the inconvenience, including cheap beers.

stories.title: Florida city cancels St. Patrick's Day parade, citing new anti-DEI law
stories.summary: A new Florida law that prohibits taxpayer dollars from going toward diversity initiatives has prompted Delray Beach to cancel its St. Patrick's Day parade after a nearly 60-year run.

stories.title: Maintenance gone awry caused nation-wide ground stop, says Transportation Secretary
stories.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy points blame toward contractor in explaining Friday's nation-wide aviation ground stop.

stories.title: US has lost measles elimination status, global health authorities say
stories.summary: The U.S. has lost its status as a country where measles is eliminated, according to researchers with direct knowledge of the deliberations at the Pan American Health Organization.

stories.title: SpaceX successfully catches Starship and makes history
stories.summary: The company's spacecraft returned to its Texas launchpad in dramatic fashion — by carefully lowering itself until two metal arms attached to the launch tower could secure it.

stories.title: Bomb found near ethanol plant in central Illinois forces evacuations
stories.summary: The bomb was discovered Friday afternoon at the BioUrja Renewables plant in Peoria. Officials say the bomb has been "rendered safe," but called it a "credible threat." The FBI is investigating.

stories.title: Estonia to close Russian border crossings after 'sabotage' attempt at drone factory
stories.summary: Estonia will close all its border crossing points with Russia from December 1, its ​foreign minister ‌said on Sunday, following a suspected ⁠sabotage attack on an Estonian defence company that Tallinn blamed on ‌Moscow.

stories.title: How did over 2,000 migrants reach the Canaries in just 48 hours?
stories.summary: Spain says nearly 2,200 migrants have arrived by boat to the Canary Islands this weekend. The strip of the Atlantic Ocean between West Africa and the Canary Islands is one of the world's deadliest migration routes – and the journey is usually made with ill-equipped dinghies and overcrowded boats. Details by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Madrid, Sarah Morris.

stories.title: Israel kills senior member of Hamas's military wing in Gaza strike
stories.summary: The Israeli military said on Sunday its forces had killed a senior member of Hamas's military wing in Gaza. The militant group confirmed the death of Samir Abu Younis, the commander of its Rafah brigade, adding that he played a prominent role in planning the October 7, 2023 attacks.

stories.title: 'Record number of women elected' to US Congress & governorships across country in midterm elections
stories.summary: Following the 2026 US midterm elections, Gavin Lee is pleased to welcome Politico Senior National Politics Reporter Lauren Fedor. She discusses the growing number of Democratic women elected to Congress and governorships, particularly mothers of young children. “There was a realisation across the map that perhaps moms were the best messenger for this,” she explains, pointing to voters' concerns about “the cost of living, affordability, how to make ends meet.”

stories.title: Iran claims drone attack on US military base in Bahrain
stories.summary: Bahrain issued two alerts of potential threats on Sunday, its first such warnings since September as blasts rocked the capital, Manama. It comes after Iran targeted an airbase in the US-allied island state, ending a long lull in strikes during the Middle East War and comes as negotiations to end the conflict remain at a stalemate, with the US maintaining its naval blockade and Iran its stranglehold over the strait of Hormuz. Story by Rachael Griffiths.

stories.title: Canaries urge government action after 2,200 migrants reach the islands in 48h
stories.summary: Spain says nearly 2,200 migrants have arrived by boat to the Canary Islands this weekend. The Spanish islands are one of the main entry points into Europe for migrants from Africa. The Spanish Interior Ministry says more than 13,000 arrived there between January and the end of last month. Details and analysis by Andrew Hilliar, FRANCE 24 international affairs editor.

stories.title: Jensen Huang: The French Connection
stories.summary: President Trump is heading to Asia in a few days time, and will meet President Putin and President Xi. There's likely to be one fewer tech giants at the table, Jensen Huang, newly resigned from Nvidia, over the suspected spy affair.

stories.title: Santa school in full swing in London ahead of Christmas celebrations
stories.summary: It may still be November but it's beginning to look a lot like Christmas in South London, as many Santa impersonators are heading to school for their festive training. The school, organised by an event company called Ministry of Fun, brings together Santas, elves, and Mrs Clauses to share experiences, practice belly laughs and learn how to bring the magic of Christmas to life. Story by Rachael Griffiths.

stories.title: A deep dive into Ivory Coast's solar energy goals
stories.summary: Can Ivory Coast, which remains heavily dependent on fossil fuels, turn to solar power to make its energy consumption greener and more sustainable? We visited the country's new solar power plant in Ferkessédougou, in the north of the country. Inaugurated in July, it is expected to generate nearly 90 gigawatt-hours of electricity a year. Report by Julia Guggenheim.

stories.title: Why the Nvidia scandal is bad news for Europe’s AI ambitions
stories.summary: Nvidia's Jensen Huang poured money into open-source AI, from French-founded Hugging Face to chips for Mistral's data centres, and fought Washington's attempts to restrict it. With Huang gone and China hawks emboldened, Tech 24 asks whether Europe's AI ambitions have lost their most powerful ally, and whether he was ever the champion Europe needed.

stories.title: Rating del sábado: cómo les fue a "La noche de Mirtha" en su nuevo horario y al debut de Moldavsky y Toto Kirzner
stories.summary: El ciclo que ahora comanda Juana Viale pasó de las 21.30 a las 22.30, como para ver si mejora su mano a mano con Andy Kusnetzoff. Los números del estreno de "Todo sigue igual", por El Trece. Los más vistos de cada canal.

stories.title: Revelan que Federico Beligoy compró un lujoso departamento en Villa Devoto una semana antes de viajar al Mundial 2026
stories.summary: Una investigación periodística de La Nación detectó que el director nacional de Arbitraje de la AFA adquirió una propiedad de 380 m2 y dos cocheras junto a su esposa. La pagó 490 mil dólares, un monto que está por debajo de los valores de mercado.

stories.title: Eurovisión Asia: Filipinas ganó la primera edición con un himno al empoderamiento femenino
stories.summary: El mayor espectáculo musical televisado en directo del mundo tuvo su debut en el continente asiático. La cantante filipina Carmelle ganó con el tema “Sobra-Sobra”: el video.

stories.title: El escándalo en Deportivo Madryn contra Maipú, por la Primera Nacional: acusación de un parte médico falso, "conmoción acústica" y el antecedente del Tribunal de Disciplina de AFA
stories.summary: El partido por la primera ronda del Reducido de la Primera Nacional en busca del segundo ascenso a la Liga Profesional fue suspendido cuando el conjunto patagónico ganaba 3 a 1 por una agresión al arquero visitante. Se espera la resolución de la AFA, cuyo presidente Chiqui Tapia tiene una relación cercana con los patagónicos.

stories.title: Tragedia en Salta: un hombre y sus tres hijas de 8, 5, y 4 años fueron encontrados muertos por insolación y deshidratación
stories.summary: El padre y las niñas habían salido en moto rumbo a Altos de la Sierra desde una localidad cercana de Formosa.

stories.title: El jefe del PRO en el Senado puso en duda que el Gobierno tenga los votos para suspender las PASO: “No lo veo tan certero”
stories.summary: Martin Goerling cuestionó el apuro del Gobierno por aprobar una reforma a pocos meses de las elecciones presidenciales. Según adelantó, el Ejecutivo presentará un nuevo dictamen el martes.

stories.title: Trump urge al Congreso aprobar más fondos para modernizar el sistema aéreo de EE.UU.
stories.summary: Trump exige al Congreso financiamiento urgente para modernizar el control aéreo tras suspensiones masivas de vuelos en EE.UU. por fallas técnicas. El secretario de Transporte descarta ciberataques y atribuye el problema a trabajos de modernización del cableado en telecomunicaciones aéreas.

stories.title: Lula confirmó que mañana se reunirá con Pedro Sánchez en Madrid, en la cuenta regresiva para las elecciones en España
stories.summary: El encuentro se realizará en el final de la gira de Lula antes de regresar a Brasil. Sánchez está en plena campaña en busca de su reelección, pero está aparece debilitado en los sondeos.

stories.title: Romeo Santos y Prince Royce hicieron bailar a Vélez: bachata, seducción y una competencia para ver quién encendía más al público
stories.summary: Los dos referentes del género desembarcaron por primera vez juntos en la Argentina con su gira Mejor Tarde Que Nunca. Ante un estadio colmado, repasaron sus carreras, presentaron temas de su primer disco compartido y desataron la euforia con los clásicos de Aventura. El pedido de disculpas de Romeo, el rey de la noche "fortinera".

stories.title: Rocío Robles reveló que su hermana desapareció al nacer en un hospital denunciado por tráfico de bebés: “No sabemos si está viva o muerta”
stories.summary: La periodista recordó las irregularidades que rodearon el parto de su mamá y las dificultades que enfrentaron para obtener respuestas. Además, contó cómo continúa la búsqueda y dejó un pedido público para dar con su paradero.

stories.title: Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza cleared of using AI to write prize-winning story
stories.summary: After a month-long investigation it was concluded that Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which won the £10,000 Caine prize, was ‘human-written’ The Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza has been cleared of using AI to write a prize-winning short story, after the prestigious Caine prize for African writers concluded that his entry was “human-written” after a month-long investigation. Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which charts the declining fortunes of a family after the father invests in fish tanks, was announced as the winner of the £10,000 prize on 6 October. Continue reading...

stories.title: Lewis Hamilton visits Egypt’s Rafah crossing and Gaza aid facilities
stories.summary: Seven-time F1 world champion tours border area and logistics warehouses operated by Egyptian Red Crescent Lewis Hamilton has visited Egypt’s Rafah border crossing with the Gaza Strip to meet organisations sending humanitarian aid to the territory. The seven-time Formula One world champion has spoken out about conflict and humanitarian crises in the region, and has called for peace. He has frequently posted on social media about children killed in Israeli airstrikes in Gaza and called for a ceasefire. Continue reading...

stories.title: Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least seven
stories.summary: President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said. The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry. Continue reading...

stories.title: How African philosophies inspired a new approach to staging film festivals in Manchester
stories.summary: See My World, an event highlighting the pan-African thought via film, poetry and dance, builds on momentum sparked by local activists and creatives African philosophies including exploring how lessons from the past can shape the present and near future have inspired a film festival coming to Manchester. See My World, a day dedicated to independent creators from across the African diaspora in the north of England, will take place at the Contact theatre on 21 November. Continue reading...

stories.title: Kenyan doomsday sect leader jailed for 200 years for murder of 190 children
stories.summary: Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history. The sentence, comprising 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years by direct homicide, came two weeks after the court in Kenya’s coastal city of Mombasa found the cult leader guilty of the crimes. Continue reading...

stories.title: Choking fires, deadly heat and devastating floods: 2026 in extreme weather
stories.summary: People around the world have contended with unprecedented weather events and their fatal effects caused by the climate catastrophe After the world’s hottest summer since records began in 1850, the death toll from extreme weather in 2026 is already in the high tens of thousands. That is a conservative estimate and is certain to rise much higher. As Cop31 continues and scientists warn that climate breakdown may be accelerating, the Guardian looks back at a year of droughts, fires and floods as a reminder that, unless the world takes urgent action to cut emissions, this disastrous year will be on

stories.title: Storm Charles causes floods and flight cancellations across southern Europe
stories.summary: Heavy rain and strong winds have also caused disruption across British Columbia, Canada, over the last week Storm Charles has brought destructive weather to the Iberian peninsula this week, particularly in Portugal and the far south of Spain. Heavy rain and strong south-westerly winds arrived first in the Portuguese island of Madeira, before the system headed towards the mainland on 11 November. A wind gust of 84.5mph (136 km/h) was recorded at Funchal airport, alongside rainfall totals reaching 355mm (13.97in) in 12 hours. stories.title: Two skulls likely belonging to enslaved people returned to Brazil after Harvard used them in eugenics studies
stories.summary: Remains believed to have belonged to Africans or Afro-Brazilians repatriated after being flown back by diplomats Two skulls, including that of a man believed to have taken part in Brazil’s greatest slave revolt but whose remains were taken to the United States and used in racist eugenics studies at Harvard University, were repatriated on Wednesday. The remains had been outside Brazil since the 19th century. One was taken about 190 years ago from Salvador, the capital of the state of Bahia; the other, about 160 years ago, from Rio de Janeiro – and were welcomed back in moving, subdued ceremonie

stories.title: Ex-member of radical Marxist group scales balcony, escapes house arrest in Argentina
stories.summary: Leonardo Bertulazzi, 74, awaiting extradition to Italy, reportedly used harness to flee custody A 74-year-old former member of Italy’s radical Marxist group the Red Brigades has escaped from house arrest in Argentina, the country’s security ministry confirmed on Wednesday, after he reportedly hid his ankle monitor inside a tube of pork and lowered himself from a fifth-floor balcony. Authorities placed Leonardo Bertulazzi under house arrest in Buenos Aires in 2024, prior to his extradition to Italy to serve a 27-year prison sentence. He had received the sentence in 1987 for joining a subversive

stories.title: Argentinian lawyer mocks UK’s sovereignty claim in Falklands oil case
stories.summary: Lawyer says Britain wrong to believe in historic doctrine that crown has sovereignty over parts of oceans Britain should not be permitted to act as a 17th-century colonial power treating the waters around the Falkland Islands as a Dominium maris Britannici, Argentina has told an international tribunal. Marcelo Kohen, representing Argentina at a hearing in Hamburg, mocked Britain for apparently believing in the historic doctrine that the British crown has sovereignty over expansive parts of the oceans.
